intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.

experiences.name: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and offers a genuine, non-commercialized cultural experience suitable for all ages.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Group family lessons are available and instructors are experienced with children as young as 5. Most families are standing on a board within the first 30 minutes, making it a thrilling and memorable experience.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional canoe rides along the lagoon. The evening show 'Ha: Breath of Life' is a spectacular finale with world-class performers.

experiences.name: Whale Watching Cruise from Ma'alaea Harbor
experiences.description: Join a family-friendly whale watching boat tour during peak humpback whale season. Expert naturalists narrate the experience as you witness majestic humpback whales breaching, tail-slapping, and nursing their calves in the warm Hawaiian waters. Tours typically last 2 hours and depart multiple times daily. Children under 3 are often free.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - No morning activities scheduled. Flight arrives early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront room. After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along the nearby beach to get your bearings. Enjoy the ocean views and let the kids splash in the waves right in front of the resort. Pick up snacks and essentials at a nearby grocery store or ABC Store to stock your room and save on meal costs throughout the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate resort area on foot. Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Hawaii's best free experiences. Head to a nearby casual plate lunch spot or food truck for an affordable first dinner featuring local Hawaiian flavors like kalua pork or teriyaki chicken.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or skip — grab fruit and snacks from a nearby grocery store upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable plate lunches or bento boxes from a local deli or ABC Store near the resort (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Local food truck or casual plate lunch restaurant near the resort. Look for 'two-scoop rice' combo plates (~$10–$15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on settling in, hydrating after the flight, and orienting yourselves. Buy a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at a grocery store to save money all week. Ask resort staff for free local maps and budget dining recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the beach directly in front of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Build sandcastles, swim, and snorkel if you brought gear (or rent affordable snorkel sets locally). This is completely free and perfect for families. Arrive early to claim a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby state beach park or public beach area for a change of scenery. Many Hawaiian state beach parks are free to enter and offer picnic tables, restrooms, and calm swimming areas ideal for families. Pack a picnic lunch from the grocery store to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local farmers market or night market if one is running nearby. These are great for affordable fresh fruit, local snacks, and cultural entertainment. Many feature live Hawaiian music at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast in the room using groceries purchased yesterday — cereal, fruit, yogurt, and juice (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch from the grocery store — sandwiches, chips, fruit, and drinks (~$5–$8 per person).
meals.dinner: Farmers market food stalls or a local Hawaiian BBQ joint. Try loco moco or spam musubi for an authentic and budget-friendly meal (~$10–$14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a family snorkel kit from a discount store like Walmart or Target if available nearby — it pays for itself within a few uses compared to daily rentals. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect both your skin and Hawaii's coral reefs.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free or low-cost hike on a scenic trail near your resort area. Many Hawaiian trails are publicly accessible and offer stunning coastal or mountain views. Look for beginner-friendly trails suitable for families with children. Bring plenty of water and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free or low-admission cultural attraction such as a historic Hawaiian heiau (temple site), a public botanical garden, or a local museum with family discounts. Many cultural sites across Hawaii are free or request only a small donation.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort beach. Many beachfront resorts host free or low-cost cultural demonstrations such as hula dancing or lei-making. Check the resort activity board for complimentary programming.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — instant oatmeal, bananas, and coffee or juice (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and a simple lunch to enjoy at a scenic overlook or picnic area on the hike (~$5–$7 per person).
meals.dinner: Find a local Hawaiian diner or family-style restaurant. Try saimin (Hawaiian noodle soup) or a plate lunch combo for an affordable and filling meal (~$10–$13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Always check trail conditions and closures before heading out, especially during summer when some areas may have high UV index. Download the AllTrails app for free trail maps. Bring a first aid kit for the kids.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local fish pond, wildlife refuge, or nature preserve near your area. Hawaii has several free natural heritage sites where families can observe native birds, sea turtles, and coastal ecosystems. This is both educational and entertaining for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a popular snorkeling beach or marine sanctuary. Many of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots are free public beaches. Rent snorkel gear locally if needed (~$10–$15/day per set) or use your own. Look for green sea turtles, colorful reef fish, and coral formations.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost community event, outdoor concert, or cultural performance. Many Hawaiian towns host weekly community gatherings with live music and local food vendors. Check local event boards or community websites.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — toast, peanut butter, fresh pineapple or papaya from the grocery store (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable poke bowls from a local grocery store deli counter — one of Hawaii's best budget food values (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Community event food vendors or a casual local restaurant. Try Hawaiian plate lunches with kalua pork, lomi salmon, and poi (~$10–$14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Poke bowls from grocery store deli counters (like Foodland or Times Supermarket) are significantly cheaper than restaurant poke and equally delicious. Sea turtle viewing is free but maintain the required 10-foot distance as required by Hawaiian law.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic coastal drive along a famous highway or coastal road near your area. Stop at free public lookout points, blow holes, or scenic overlooks. This is a great way to see diverse landscapes without spending much — just gas money if you have a rental car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a free or low-cost beach along the coastal drive for swimming and relaxation. Pack a full picnic lunch and spend a couple of hours enjoying a quieter, less-touristy stretch of coastline. Look for tide pools for the kids to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a quiet beach evening. Stargaze from the beach after dark — Hawaii's skies are remarkably clear and light pollution is low in many areas. This is a completely free and magical family experience.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — granola bars, fruit, and juice to eat on the go before the drive (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at a scenic beach stop along the coastal drive — sandwiches, chips, fruit, and cold drinks from a cooler (~$5–$8 per person).
meals.dinner: Local pizza place, burger joint, or casual family restaurant back near the resort. Look for early-bird specials or family meal deals (~$10–$15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: If renting a car, compare prices from multiple agencies and book in advance for the best rates. Gas up at Costco if you have a membership — gas is significantly cheaper there. A small cooler from a dollar store is a great investment for picnic days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a free public botanical garden, arboretum, or tropical plant preserve. Hawaii has extraordinary flora, and many public gardens are free or have very low admission. Kids will enjoy seeing exotic plants, colorful birds, and tropical landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a calm, family-friendly lagoon or bay beach for an afternoon of swimming and relaxation. Many of Hawaii's best swimming spots are at county or state beach parks with free parking and facilities. Bring your own floats and beach toys.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a family movie night on the beach if your resort or a nearby venue offers an outdoor movie screening — many Hawaiian resorts and parks host these for free or low cost. Alternatively, enjoy a bonfire-style evening on the beach if permitted.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — scrambled eggs if you have a kitchenette, or cereal and fruit (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Shave ice and plate lunch from a local roadside stand or food truck near the botanical garden (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Casual beachside restaurant or resort casual dining. Look for happy hour specials on appetizers to keep costs down (~$12–$16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Shave ice is a Hawaiian tradition and an affordable treat — look for stands that offer it with azuki beans and ice cream inside for the full local experience. Many botanical gardens are free on specific days of the week, so check schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free guided nature walk or self-guided interpretive trail at a state park. Many Hawaiian state parks offer free ranger-led programs on weekends, covering local ecology, history, and culture. These are excellent educational experiences for children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Hawaiian cultural center or historic district. Walk through historic downtown areas, view traditional Hawaiian architecture, and browse local shops. Many cultural centers offer free exhibits or low-cost family programs.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a traditional Hawaiian luau experience — look for community luaus or smaller local versions rather than the large commercial resort luaus, which can be very expensive. Some community centers host luaus at a fraction of the resort price (~$30–$50 per person vs. $100+).

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — pancake mix if you have a kitchenette, or muffins and fruit from the grocery store (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Affordable bento box or plate lunch from a local deli in the historic district (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Community or local luau if attending, which typically includes food. If not, cook a simple meal in the room or grab affordable Hawaiian BBQ from a local spot (~$15–$25 per person for luau, $10–$14 otherwise).

day_by_day.notes: Research community luau options well in advance as they often require reservations. If a full luau is outside the budget, look for free hula performances at shopping centers or cultural events — these are common throughout Hawaii and give a taste of the culture without the cost.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a full morning at the beach trying a new water activity. Look for affordable group lessons or demos for stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) or bodyboarding. Group lessons are significantly cheaper than private ones (~$20–$30 per person). Kids typically love bodyboarding with a rented board (~$5–$10/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free aquarium, marine education center, or tide pool area. Many Hawaiian communities have free or low-cost marine education facilities. Alternatively, explore a rocky tide pool area where kids can observe starfish, sea urchins, and small fish up close.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a meal together as a family using local ingredients from the farmers market or grocery store. Pick up fresh fish, tropical fruits, and local produce for a memorable and very affordable Hawaiian-inspired dinner in or near your room.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — fresh tropical fruit bowl with yogurt and granola (~$4–$6 per person).
meals.lunch: Affordable food truck lunch near the beach or water activity area. Try fish tacos, garlic shrimp plates, or acai bowls (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: DIY dinner using local groceries — grilled fish, rice, macaroni salad, and fresh pineapple. Use a resort BBQ grill if available (~$8–$12 per person total).

day_by_day.notes: Many Hawaiian beach parks have free public BBQ grills available on a first-come, first-served basis. Garlic shrimp trucks on the North Shore (if accessible) are a legendary and affordable Hawaiian food experience — typically $13–$16 for a full plate with rice.

day_by_day.morning: Take a final scenic hike to a waterfall, crater, or viewpoint that you haven't visited yet. Choose a trail appropriate for your family's fitness level. Many of Hawaii's most iconic viewpoints are accessible via free public trails with minimal hiking experience required.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon souvenir shopping at local markets, craft fairs, or discount shops rather than resort gift shops. Look for locally made items like macadamia nut products, Hawaiian sea salt, locally grown coffee, and handmade jewelry — these are more authentic and often cheaper when bought directly from local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy one final special beach sunset as a family. Reflect on the trip's highlights and let the kids play in the waves one last time. Take lots of photos. Head to a slightly nicer casual restaurant for a celebratory last full dinner without completely breaking the budget.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — use up remaining groceries to minimize waste and save money (~$3–$5 per person).
meals.lunch: Affordable plate lunch or food truck meal near the shopping area (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated casual dining experience for a trip celebration — look for a local seafood shack or Hawaiian family restaurant with fresh catch of the day (~$15–$20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: For souvenirs, Costco Hawaii locations carry excellent local products like Kona coffee and macadamia nuts at significantly lower prices than airport or resort shops. Avoid buying anything labeled 'Made in Hawaii' without verifying — look for 'Grown in Hawaii' or 'Made by a Hawaiian artisan' for authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on the beach — completely free and absolutely unforgettable. Pack your bags and check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the concierge if your flight is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final few hours near the resort area. Take a last swim, walk the beach, or grab shave ice one more time. Head to the airport with plenty of time, accounting for Hawaii's traffic patterns and security wait times.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Use any remaining local cash or gift cards at the airport for snacks. Reflect on an amazing 10-day budget Hawaii adventure with the family.

meals.breakfast: Final in-room or resort breakfast — use up any remaining groceries or grab a quick bite at a nearby café (~$4–$8 per person).
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch near the resort or at the airport. Pack snacks from the grocery store for the flight to avoid expensive airport food (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal. Pack homemade snacks and sandwiches to save on airport prices if possible (~$10–$15 per person if eating at airport).

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before an international flight. Use any remaining Hawaiian cash on local snacks or small gifts at the airport rather than exchanging it back. Take one last deep breath of the Hawaiian air — a budget trip to Hawaii is still one of the most magical experiences in the world!

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

Tours typically last 2 hours and depart multiple times daily. Children under 3 are often free.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront). After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented. Dip your toes in the ocean and enjoy the resort pool with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate resort area and nearby shops. Watch the sunset from the beach — a perfect low-key introduction to Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the airport or on the flight before landing.
meals.lunch: Light snack or casual bite at the airport upon arrival or a quick stop near the resort.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — try the fresh catch of the day and local poke bowls to kick off the Hawaiian food experience.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to combat jet lag and travel fatigue. Unpack, hydrate, and let the family decompress. Pick up any beach essentials (sunscreen, snacks, water bottles) at a nearby ABC Store or convenience shop.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Waikiki Beach for Beginner Surfing Lessons with certified instructors. The gentle, rolling waves make this ideal for all ages and skill levels. Lessons typically run 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Waikiki Beach after the lesson — build sandcastles, swim, or rent a bodyboard. Explore the Waikiki promenade and browse local shops along Kalakaua Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Waikiki for dinner, then enjoy a free beachside performance — Waikiki often has live music and hula shows at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, family-friendly).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a smoothie bowl from a nearby café like Bogart's Café.
meals.lunch: Grab a plate lunch (classic Hawaiian comfort food) from a local food truck near Waikiki — try spam musubi, macaroni salad, and teriyaki chicken.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — iconic mid-range oceanfront restaurant with fresh seafood, burgers, and a great family atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Book surfing lessons in advance to secure family slots. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously — the Hawaiian sun is strong even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to Hanauma Bay for Snorkeling. Arrive early (by 7:30–8:00 AM) to beat crowds and secure entry — the bay has a daily visitor cap. Watch the required marine education video before entering the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Hanauma Bay by early afternoon. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout and Sandy Beach on the way back for scenic views and a quick stretch.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Let the kids enjoy the pool while parents unwind. Optional: visit a nearby shave ice stand for a classic Hawaiian treat.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort or pack granola bars and fruit to eat on the go before Hanauma Bay.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at Hanauma Bay's picnic area (no outside food allowed on the beach, but the pavilion area is fine) or grab food at their small concession stand.
meals.dinner: Kaimana Farm Café or a local family-friendly Hawaiian restaurant near the resort — try laulau (pork wrapped in taro leaves) or kalua pig.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are REQUIRED and must be booked online in advance. Bring water shoes for rocky reef areas. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site. No sunscreen with harmful chemicals — reef-safe only.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to the Polynesian Cultural Center — depart early (by 8:30 AM) as it's about a 1-hour drive to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring the six authentic Polynesian villages (Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga). Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center villages. Catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the river — a spectacular free-flowing cultural show included with admission.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class Polynesian performance with stunning costumes, fire dancing, and live music. One of the most memorable family experiences in Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing.
meals.lunch: Ali'i Luau buffet lunch at the Polynesian Cultural Center (included in some packages) or the Gateway Buffet — a great spread of Polynesian and Hawaiian dishes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center's evening show package, or stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck on the North Shore for the famous garlic shrimp on the drive back.

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance — combo packages with the evening show offer the best value. The full-day experience runs roughly 12:00–9:30 PM, so an early start is key. This is one of the most highly recommended family activities in all of Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow resort morning. Swim at the resort beach, play in the sand, or try resort amenities like paddleboarding or kayaking (often available for guests).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument for a family hike. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail is moderate and leads to a stunning panoramic view of Honolulu and Waikiki. Takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip.
day_by_day.evening: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau (if on Maui) — NOTE: If the resort is on Oahu, substitute with a local luau such as the Paradise Cove Luau or Germaine's Luau, both family-friendly and authentic with hula dancing, imu ceremony, and traditional Hawaiian feast.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — try açaí bowls or loco moco (a Hawaiian breakfast classic with rice, egg, and gravy).
meals.lunch: Picnic near Diamond Head or grab a bite at Kapiolani Park — nearby food trucks and vendors are plentiful.
meals.dinner: Luau dinner included with the luau package — a full traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, haupia (coconut pudding), and more.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires a small entry fee and advance reservations are recommended. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for the hike and bring water. The luau is a highlight of any Hawaii trip — book well in advance as it sells out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural history and cultural museum. Fascinating exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, volcanology, and Pacific Island cultures. Great for curious kids and adults alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a beautiful, calm, family-friendly beach just minutes from Waikiki. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on the wide sandy shore. Less crowded than Waikiki.
day_by_day.evening: Browse Ala Moana Center — one of the largest open-air shopping malls in the world, right next to the beach. Great for souvenirs, local brands, and casual dining.

meals.breakfast: Café Kaila or similar local breakfast spot — known for creative pancakes and Hawaiian-style breakfast plates.
meals.lunch: Mariposa Restaurant at Neiman Marcus in Ala Moana or grab a casual poke bowl from Foodland Farms nearby.
meals.dinner: Yardhouse or a mid-range restaurant at Ala Moana Center — good variety of cuisines suitable for families.

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is educational and air-conditioned — a nice break from the sun. Ala Moana Beach Park has lifeguards on duty and calm waters perfect for younger children.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor Historic Sites. A deeply moving and educational experience for older children and adults. Book tickets in advance — the boat tour to the memorial is free but timed entry passes are required.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Battleship Missouri Memorial and the Pacific Aviation Museum on Ford Island — included in combo ticket packages and highly engaging for kids who love history and aircraft.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a sunset beach walk and let the family reflect on the day's experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before heading to Pearl Harbor (aim to arrive by 8:00–8:30 AM).
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor Visitor Center has a café — grab sandwiches, salads, or a quick hot meal on-site.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood or a local Hawaiian plate lunch spot near the resort — keep it casual and affordable after a full day.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is one of the most visited sites in Hawaii — arrive early to avoid long lines. Bags must be checked (no large bags allowed in the memorial area). This experience is best for children aged 8 and up who can appreciate the historical significance.

day_by_day.morning: North Shore Adventure Day — drive up to the famous North Shore of Oahu. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park for swimming (calmer in summer). Stop at Sunset Beach and Banzai Pipeline to see the legendary surf spots even if waves are small in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Waimea Valley — a beautiful botanical garden and nature park with a stunning waterfall at the end of a 1.5-mile walk. Swimming at Waimea Falls is allowed (life jackets provided). A magical family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back along the scenic Kamehameha Highway. Stop in Haleiwa Town — the charming surf town of the North Shore — for shave ice at Matsumoto's (a legendary institution) and browse local art galleries and boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua (a local favorite) on the way to the North Shore.
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku — the famous garlic butter shrimp plate is a North Shore must-eat.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Haleiwa at Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — great mid-range seafood with a laid-back vibe.

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 1–1.5 hours from Waikiki. Start early to make the most of the day. In August, ocean conditions are generally calm and safe for swimming. Waimea Valley charges a small admission fee.

day_by_day.morning: Whale Watching Cruise — NOTE: Humpback whale season in Hawaii peaks January–March, so August sightings are unlikely. Substitute with a family-friendly Catamaran Sailing and Snorkel Cruise departing from Waikiki or Honolulu Harbor. These tours typically include snorkeling, dolphin spotting, and stunning coastal views. Depart around 9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the cruise by midday. Spend the afternoon at Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches with powdery white sand and turquoise water. Great for kayaking to the Mokulua Islands.
day_by_day.evening: Final big family dinner — celebrate the trip with a special meal. Return to the resort for a bonfire or stargazing on the beach if available.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the morning cruise.
meals.lunch: Lunch is often included on catamaran cruise packages — fresh fruit, sandwiches, and drinks on board.
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua — a beloved local institution with great steaks, fresh fish, and a warm family atmosphere. A perfect celebratory dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran cruise in advance. If whale watching is a must, consider this trip between January and March for guaranteed sightings. Kailua Beach is on the windward side of Oahu — about 30–40 minutes from Waikiki. Parking can be limited on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy one last swim at the resort beach or pool. Pack up and check out. Do a final souvenir run at a nearby shop or the International Marketplace in Waikiki.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit the Honolulu Museum of Art for a quick cultural stop, or simply relax at a nearby café. Head to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of Hawaii home with you. Mahalo!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out with a full Hawaiian spread: fresh tropical fruit, macadamia nut pancakes, Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Quick and easy — Rainbow Drive-In near the airport, a beloved local institution serving classic plate lunches since 1961. Perfect last Hawaiian meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the destination airport.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort if a late checkout is possible. Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Don't forget to declare any food items (like macadamia nuts or fresh fruit) at customs if required by your destination country.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.

experiences.name: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and offers a genuine, non-commercialized cultural experience suitable for all ages.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Group family lessons are available and instructors are experienced with children as young as 5. Most families are standing on a board within the first 30 minutes, making it a thrilling and memorable experience.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional canoe rides along the lagoon. The evening show 'Ha: Breath of Life' is a spectacular finale with world-class performers.

experiences.name: Whale Watching Cruise from Ma'alaea Harbor
experiences.description: Join a family-friendly whale watching boat tour during peak humpback whale season. Expert naturalists narrate the experience as you witness majestic humpback whales breaching, tail-slapping, and nursing their calves in the warm Hawaiian waters. Tours typically last 2 hours and depart multiple times daily. Children under 3 are often free.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs and collect luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the resort's private beach to acclimate. Enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation with your personal concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from your beachfront terrace or the resort's oceanfront infinity pool. Light exploration of the resort grounds and amenities.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or light snack at airport
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant. Indulge in fresh Hawaiian seafood — recommended: grilled ono with mango salsa, paired with a local craft cocktail. Enjoy the sound of waves as the sun sets over the Pacific.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in through the concierge in advance. Tip: Set clocks to Hawaii Standard Time (UTC-10) and hydrate well after the long flight. Ask the concierge to pre-book all upcoming experiences tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a private guided Snorkeling session at the resort's beachfront reef. Explore colorful tropical fish and coral in calm, family-friendly waters with a certified marine guide who provides premium equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. A private guided tour ensures skip-the-line access. Crystal-clear waters teeming with sea turtles, parrotfish, and vibrant coral make this a bucket-list family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour on the beach. Enjoy a curated charcuterie and tropical fruit board delivered to your beachfront suite terrace.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's garden terrace restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, açaí bowls, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef — gourmet sandwiches, fresh poke bowls, chilled juices, and tropical desserts served in a private shaded cabana.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a nearby upscale farm-to-table restaurant featuring locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients — recommended: macadamia-crusted mahi-mahi with taro purée and a curated Hawaiian wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and has limited daily entry — your concierge should secure this. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Best snorkeling visibility is typically in the morning hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private beginner Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach with certified instructors. The gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki are perfect for all ages. Private lessons ensure personalized attention for every family member. Premium boards, rash guards, and all equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, stroll along the Waikiki promenade. Visit the upscale shops at the Royal Hawaiian Center and explore the iconic pink Royal Hawaiian Hotel grounds. Optional: rent a private outrigger canoe for a 45-minute guided paddle along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a vibrant evening in Waikiki — visit a rooftop bar for panoramic ocean views and craft cocktails before dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered to your beachfront terrace — fresh-squeezed juices, Hawaiian sweet bread French toast, local fruit platters, and Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-surf lunch at a premium beachside restaurant in Waikiki — fresh poke bowls, lobster tacos, and coconut shrimp with ocean views.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a celebrated Waikiki restaurant — recommended: tasting menu featuring locally caught sashimi, wagyu beef, and a Hawaiian-inspired dessert course with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book private surf lessons in advance — group sizes are strictly limited for the premium experience. Waikiki can be busy; your concierge can arrange a private driver to navigate parking and traffic seamlessly.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip begins with a morning departure. Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Enjoy live cultural demonstrations, traditional crafts, and storytelling with a private VIP guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Polynesian Cultural Center experience — watch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon, participate in hands-on activities like fire-making and weaving, and enjoy the immersive cultural exhibits. VIP access ensures priority seating and behind-the-scenes experiences.
day_by_day.evening: The Grand Polynesian Luau at the Cultural Center — a breathtaking evening show with world-class Polynesian performers, traditional music, fire dancing, and a premium buffet dinner featuring Hawaiian favorites.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — continental spread with fresh pastries, tropical fruits, yogurt parfaits, and coffee before departure.
meals.lunch: Premium lunch included with the VIP Cultural Center package — traditional Hawaiian plate lunch featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, and haupia dessert.
meals.dinner: Grand Luau premium buffet dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — feast on roasted meats, fresh seafood, tropical salads, and traditional Hawaiian desserts under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from Waikiki — arrange a private luxury van or chauffeured vehicle for the family. VIP packages include reserved seating, priority access, and exclusive backstage experiences. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation morning at the resort. Enjoy a private family yoga session on the beach at sunrise led by a certified instructor, followed by a dip in the resort's infinity pool. Optional: schedule a family spa session at the resort's luxury spa — Hawaiian lomi lomi massages are highly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private catamaran sailing charter along the coastline. Snorkel at a secluded reef accessible only by boat, spot sea turtles, and enjoy a champagne and canapé service on deck. The crew provides premium snorkel gear, paddleboards, and water toys.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a golden-hour beach walk. Enjoy a private bonfire experience on the beach arranged by the resort — complete with s'mores, Hawaiian storytelling, and stargazing with a telescope.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet resort breakfast at the beachfront restaurant — eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, avocado toast on Hawaiian sourdough, and freshly blended tropical smoothies.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served aboard the private catamaran — fresh sashimi, artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, chilled rosé, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Intimate private beachfront dinner arranged by the resort — a dedicated chef prepares a custom 5-course tasting menu on the sand with tiki torches, fresh flowers, and ocean breezes.

day_by_day.notes: The private catamaran charter should be booked at least 3–5 days in advance. Lomi lomi spa appointments fill quickly — ask the concierge to reserve immediately upon arrival. The private beach dinner is a memorable splurge and ideal for a special family moment.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter tour of the island — a breathtaking aerial perspective of volcanic craters, lush valleys, cascading waterfalls, and the stunning Pacific coastline. A private helicopter with a knowledgeable pilot-guide provides an unforgettable family experience with panoramic views unavailable from the ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a luxury botanical garden for a private guided tour — discover rare tropical plants, orchids, and the rich biodiversity of Hawaii's native flora. Followed by a visit to a premium Hawaiian chocolate or coffee farm for a tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Luau at Old Lahaina Luau — one of Hawaii's most authentic and celebrated luaus. Experience hula dancing, imu (underground oven) ceremony, fire knife dancing, and a feast of traditional Hawaiian cuisine in an intimate, culturally rich setting.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit, granola, yogurt, and juices to avoid discomfort during the helicopter tour.
meals.lunch: Farm-fresh lunch at the coffee or chocolate farm — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, macadamia nut treats, and freshly brewed Kona coffee or cacao drinks.
meals.dinner: Traditional Hawaiian feast at Old Lahaina Luau — kalua pig, poi, lomi lomi salmon, fresh fish, haupia, and tropical beverages in an oceanfront setting.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours should be booked well in advance and are weather-dependent — confirm the morning of. Old Lahaina Luau is one of the most sought-after luau experiences in Hawaii; reservations are essential and often sell out weeks ahead. Dress in light, comfortable aloha attire.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Whale Watching Cruise from Ma'alaea Harbor (August is late season but occasional sightings of other marine life remain excellent). A family-friendly luxury boat tour with expert naturalist guides — spot dolphins, sea turtles, flying fish, and possibly humpback whales. Premium vessel with comfortable seating, sun decks, and onboard naturalist commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cruise, explore the charming harbor town. Visit the Maui Ocean Center — one of the finest aquariums in the Pacific — for an immersive family experience with sharks, rays, jellyfish, and Hawaiian sea life exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drive along a scenic coastal road. Stop at a lookout point for golden-hour photography before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — continental spread, fresh juices, and coffee to go.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served aboard the whale watching vessel — fresh sandwiches, tropical salads, fruit, and beverages included in the premium package.
meals.dinner: Upscale dinner at a celebrated oceanfront restaurant — recommended: fresh catch of the day prepared tableside, paired with a curated Hawaiian craft beer or wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: August is toward the end of peak humpback season — sightings are possible but not guaranteed. However, dolphin and sea turtle encounters are very common year-round. The Maui Ocean Center admission is highly recommended for families with children. Book the premium whale watching vessel rather than a standard tour boat.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike to a stunning coastal or waterfall trail suited for families — a knowledgeable local guide leads the way through lush tropical jungle, sharing stories of Hawaiian history, native plants, and wildlife. Premium gear, trekking poles, and cold towels provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed afternoon. Enjoy the resort's private beach — build sandcastles, play in the waves, or simply lounge under a private cabana with chilled beverages and fresh fruit delivered by beach attendants.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Hawaiian cultural workshop at the resort — learn traditional lei making, ukulele basics, and hula dancing as a family in an intimate setting led by a local cultural ambassador.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast before the hike — protein-rich options including eggs, avocado, smoked meats, whole-grain toast, and fresh juices.
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at a local hidden gem restaurant — fresh island-style fish tacos, açaí bowls, and tropical smoothies.
meals.dinner: Elegant resort dinner at the premium restaurant — multi-course Hawaiian fusion menu with locally sourced ingredients, paired with a curated wine or sake selection.

day_by_day.notes: Choose a hike appropriate for all family members' fitness levels — your concierge can match the trail difficulty to your group. Wear sturdy footwear, apply sunscreen, and bring insect repellent. The cultural workshop in the evening is a wonderful way to connect with Hawaiian traditions in a relaxed, family-friendly setting.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury beach day — the ultimate resort indulgence. Reserve a premium private cabana on the resort's beachfront with dedicated butler service. Enjoy paddleboarding, kayaking, and snorkeling equipment available exclusively for resort guests. Optional: book a private underwater photography session with a professional photographer to capture family memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby luxury shopping district or open-air market — browse premium Hawaiian jewelry, artwork, and locally crafted souvenirs. Visit a gallery featuring works by renowned Hawaiian artists for a unique cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration — arrange a private sunset cocktail cruise for the family aboard a luxury catamaran. Watch the sun dip below the Pacific horizon with champagne, artisan canapés, and live acoustic Hawaiian music performed on deck.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-suite breakfast — full cooked spread delivered to your beachfront terrace, including eggs Benedict, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, smoked salmon, and Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Beachside gourmet lunch at the resort cabana — fresh lobster rolls, sushi platter, chilled gazpacho, and premium beverages served by your personal butler.
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — premium tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the best of Hawaiian cuisine: fresh sashimi, Kona lobster, grass-fed beef, and a decadent dessert finale.

day_by_day.notes: The private underwater photography session requires advance booking and is a priceless keepsake. The sunset cocktail cruise is an ideal way to close the trip on a high note — confirm the booking 48 hours in advance and communicate any dietary preferences for the canapé menu.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk — a peaceful, unhurried stroll along the shoreline to soak in the last moments of Hawaii's natural beauty. Optional: one final dip in the ocean or a quiet meditation session on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to the airport. Allow ample time for check-in and departure procedures. Browse the airport's premium duty-free shops for last-minute Hawaiian gifts — Kona coffee, macadamia chocolates, and local honey make excellent souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Hawaii — carry beautiful memories of ten extraordinary days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final lavish resort breakfast — order your favorite dishes from the past ten days. Savor the last cup of Kona coffee with an ocean view.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a quick stop at a quality airport restaurant — fresh poke bowl or Hawaiian plate lunch as a final taste of the islands.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your layover destination.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort concierge to maximize your final morning. Pack any perishable Hawaiian food items (fresh fruit, certain foods) carefully — some items cannot be taken off the island due to agricultural regulations. Confirm your return flight details the night before and arrange the airport transfer in advance. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!
